criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: API keys were piped from BENCH_API_KEYS into a Railway variable without being printed. DATABASE_URL is a Railway reference variable, and the project token sits in a chmod-600 .env that .gitignore and .railwayignore exclude. The only gap: raw API keys are stored as plaintext in the owner_key column.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The running code came from the agent's own directory through `railway up`, built by Railpack with 0 audit findings. But the runtime resolved to Node 20.20.2, which has been end-of-life since April 2026, because engines says only ">=20". Dependencies use caret ranges, and the base and Postgres images are floating tags rather than digests.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a personal side project on Railway's usage-based plan (Hobby, probably). Railway's terms allow personal use and its services don't sleep. The exact account plan wasn't visible, so this is inferred.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The app reaches Postgres over the private network and only the web service has a domain. The Railpack container runs as root by default. The official Postgres template usually adds a public TCP proxy, and the agent didn't check or remove it; this couldn't be verified without credentials.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: Plain HTTP gets a 301 to HTTPS, and the Let's Encrypt certificate is valid. The app sets no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP, and Railway's edge doesn't add them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Probes for .env, .git, package.json, source files, /admin and /debug all returned a JSON 404. Malformed JSON gets a generic 400 with no stack trace, and the only public routes are the ones the spec requires.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Queries are parameterized, input types are validated, notes are scoped to their owner (other keys get 404), docs HTML is escaped, and a per-key limit of 60 requests a minute returns Retry-After. The weak spots: requests with a missing or invalid key aren't rate limited, JSON bodies up to 1 MB are parsed before authentication, and title, content and tags have no length limits.

findings.title: Production runs end-of-life Node.js 20
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md `railway up` output: 'mise ✓ node@20.20.2'. app/package.json engines: "node": ">=20". app/STACK.md says 'Node.js 22+'. Node 20 reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30.
findings.recommendation: Pin a supported LTS, e.g. "engines": {"node": "22.x"} or a .node-version file, and redeploy.

findings.title: Build inputs not pinned by digest or exact version
findings.evidence: app/package.json uses "express": "^5.3.0" and "pg": "^8.23.1". The Railpack base image is platform-chosen, and the Postgres template uses ghcr.io/railwayapp-templates/postgres-ssl:18 (tag, not digest). A package-lock.json was generated during the build (process/build.md) but isn't in the reviewed app/ tree.
findings.recommendation: Commit package-lock.json so the build runs npm ci, and pin the Postgres image (and ideally the builder image) by digest.

findings.title: Postgres template may expose a public TCP proxy
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: the DB was deployed from template 'postgres' via templateDeployV2 with an unmodified serializedConfig (truncated in the log), and no networking settings were checked afterward. The official template usually adds a public TCP proxy (DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL). The app only uses the private DATABASE_URL.
findings.recommendation: Remove the TCP proxy from adb-8ivox-api-db so Postgres is reachable only over Railway's private network.

findings.title: App container runs as root
findings.evidence: Railpack build with no user configuration (app/railway.json builder RAILPACK, no Dockerfile). Railpack images run as root by default.
findings.recommendation: Use a Dockerfile with a non-root USER (e.g. node), or configure the builder to run the process as an unprivileged user.

findings.title: Missing security headers
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-8ivox-api-web-production.up.railway.app/docs returns only content-type, etag, server and x-railway-* headers: no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy.
findings.recommendation: Add helmet, or set these headers in a small Express middleware.

findings.title: Unauthenticated requests are not rate limited and bodies are parsed before auth
findings.evidence: app/src/app.js:47 runs express.json({limit:'1mb'}) globally before the /v1 auth middleware, and the rate limiter (app/src/app.js:62) only runs for valid keys. `curl -X POST /v1/notes -d '{bad'` with no key returned 400 'Malformed JSON body' instead of 401, so the body was parsed first.
findings.recommendation: Mount the JSON parser after authentication, add a coarse per-IP limit for 401s, and cap title, content and tag lengths.

findings.title: API keys stored in plaintext as note owner
findings.evidence: app/src/db.js: owner_key TEXT NOT NULL, filled with req.apiKey in app/src/app.js (INSERT ... owner_key). Anyone who can read the database learns the valid API keys.
findings.recommendation: Store a SHA-256 hash, or another stable identifier for each key, instead of the raw key.

findings.title: Rate limit state is in memory
findings.evidence: app/src/rateLimit.js keeps a Map of timestamps per key. Counters reset on redeploy and wouldn't be shared across replicas (noted in process/deployment.json).
findings.recommendation: Fine for one replica. Move the counters to Postgres or Redis if the service is ever scaled out.

security.summary: The Notes API is a small Express 5 + Postgres service on Railway, and it is soundly built: secrets go through Railway variables and reference variables and were never printed, queries are parameterized, notes are isolated per key, nothing extra is exposed, and HTTPS is enforced with a valid certificate. The main weaknesses are in the deployment: it runs on Node 20, which is end-of-life, with unpinned build inputs, a root container and a database template whose public TCP proxy was never checked. The app also sets no security headers and doesn't rate limit unauthenticated requests.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: Managed Postgres is a durable store that meets the persistence requirement, Express and pg cover the HTTP and data layers, and the hand-written OpenAPI document plus a self-contained /docs page meet the spec. The in-memory limiter is adequate for a single replica.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: There are two runtime dependencies and two services, with no extra frameworks, caches or queues. That is about as lean as a persistent, authenticated API can be.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: A long-running Node service built by Railpack, Railway's Postgres template with a volume, and reference variables over the private network are exactly what Railway does well. The build did depart from STACK.md, which said 'Node.js 22+', by landing on Node 20.

stack_fit.summary: Node.js with Express 5 and Railway-managed Postgres is a simple, well-reasoned fit for a small persistent JSON API on Railway, and STACK.md justifies it clearly. The one departure is the unpinned Node version, which resolved to Node 20, now end-of-life.

light.basis: memory billed all month, CPU for ~10 h of activity, 0.04 GB egress at $0.05/GB

busy.basis: memory billed all month, CPU for ~730 h of activity, 52.6 GB egress at $0.05/GB

final_messages.build:
I've built the Notes API and checked every requirement locally. The automated tests (4 of them) pass against a real Postgres, and I ran each requirement by hand with curl against the actual server. No servers are left running and I removed the local Postgres container.

**Stack:** Node.js with Express 5, storing notes in PostgreSQL. On Railway that will be a managed Postgres service connected through `DATABASE_URL`. `STACK.md` compares this with FastAPI + Postgres and with SQLite on a Railway volume. I chose this one for its small dependency footprint and because managed Postgres is the most reliable way to keep data through restarts and redeploys.

**What the curl checks covered:**
- `/health`, `/openapi.json` and `/docs` all respond without a key.
- A missing or unknown key gets `401`.
- Create, list, get, update and delete all work, and the list comes back newest first.
- The `tag` filter works.
- Bad input gets `400`, including a missing or empty title, wrong types and malformed JSON.
- Another key's notes return `404`.
- A note was still there after restarting the server.
- The 61st request in a minute gets `429` with `Retry-After`, and other keys are unaffected.

**Behaviours you might not assume from the spec:**
- **Rate limit memory:** the per-key counts are kept in memory. That's fine with one instance on Railway, but they reset when the app restarts and aren't shared if you run more than one instance.
- **Optional `content`:** a note can be created with only a title; `content` then defaults to `""`.
- **Empty `PATCH`:** a `PATCH` with none of `title`, `content` or `tags` gets `400`.
- **Table setup:** the server creates the table itself at startup and retries while the database comes up.

**How to run it:**
```sh
docker run -d --name notes-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16-alpine
npm install
DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres API_KEYS=key-one,key-two npm start   # port from PORT, default 3000
DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres npm test
```

For step 2, Railway only needs `DATABASE_URL` pointed at its Postgres service and `API_KEYS` set; the start command is `npm start`. The code is in `src/` (`app.js` holds the routes), the tests are in `test/api.test.js`, and `README.md` repeats these run instructions.
final_messages.deploy:
The Notes API is live at **https://adb-8ivox-api-web-production.up.railway.app**. I tested every requirement in `TASK.md` through that URL and all of them passed. No step needed a person, so `human_steps` is empty.

**What's running in the Railway project `adb-8ivox-api`:**
- **`adb-8ivox-api-web`:** the Node app, built from this directory and served over HTTPS on a Railway domain. `API_KEYS` is set to exactly the 2 keys in `BENCH_API_KEYS`.
- **`adb-8ivox-api-db`:** Railway's standard Postgres, storing its data on the volume `adb-8ivox-api-db-volume`. The app reaches it over Railway's private network.
- **`adb-8ivox-api-token`:** a project token I created and saved to `.env` (along with the project and environment IDs). That file isn't deployed and no secrets were printed.

Estimated cost is about $5/month, which is usage-based and usually covered by the Hobby plan's included usage.

**Checked through the public URL:**
- `/health`, `/openapi.json` and `/docs` respond without a key.
- A missing or unknown key gets `401`.
- Creating, listing, filtering by tag, getting, updating and deleting notes all work.
- An empty title gets `400`.
- One key gets `404` for another key's notes.
- The 61st request in a minute gets `429` with `Retry-After`, and the other key is unaffected.
- A note I created was still there after a redeploy.

**Things to know:**
- **Rate limit memory:** the per-key counts are kept in memory, so keep the web service at one instance. The counts also reset whenever it redeploys.
- **Limit used up in testing:** testing used the second benchmark key's full minute of requests, around 00:54 UTC. It reset a minute later.
- **Extra database cleaned up:** the Railway CLI can't work with the workspace token, so I created everything through Railway's API and uploaded the code with the project token. An early CLI attempt reported an error but still created a stray `Postgres` service. I deleted it and its volume.
- **`deploy.sh` removed:** I deleted the `deploy.sh` from the previous step, because it relied on that CLI path and no longer matched how the deploy works.

deployment_manifest.notes: Usage cost for a small idle Node service + Postgres is roughly $3-5/month and is typically covered by the Hobby plan's included $5 usage. API_KEYS is set to exactly BENCH_API_KEYS (2 keys); DATABASE_URL references ${{adb-8ivox-api-db.DATABASE_URL}} over the private network. Verified via the public URL: /health, /openapi.json, /docs, 401 on missing/unknown key, create/list/tag filter/get/patch/delete, 400 validation, 404 cross-key isolation, 429 with Retry-After after 60 req/min per key (other key unaffected), and data persisting across a redeploy. Rate limiting is in-memory: keep the web service at 1 replica; counters reset on redeploy. During setup the CLI accidentally created an extra 'Postgres' service; it and its volume were deleted. The workspace token cannot be used by the Railway CLI (it needs a user token), so infrastructure was created via the GraphQL API and code uploaded with `railway up` using the project token.
